ei.title: Parents' Praise Improves Preschoolers' Confidence and Self-esteem
ei.subject: 6월_2023 고1 모의고사
ei.lesson: Parents' Praise Improves Preschoolers' Confidence and Self-esteem

fullPassage: Although praise is one of the most powerful tools available for improving young children's behavior, it is equally powerful for improving your child's self-esteem. Preschoolers believe what their parents tell them in a very profound way. They do not yet have the cognitive sophistication to reason analytically and reject false information. If a preschool boy consistently hears from his mother that he is smart and a good helper, he is likely to incorporate that information into his self-image. Thinking of himself as a boy who is smart and knows how to do things is likely to make him endure longer in problem-solving efforts and increase his confidence in trying new and difficult tasks. Similarly, thinking of himself as the kind of boy who is a good helper will make him more likely to volunteer to help with tasks at home and at preschool.

questions.passage: Although praise is one of the most powerful tools ①<u>available</u> for improving young children's behavior, it is equally powerful for improving your child's self-esteem. Preschoolers believe what their parents tell them in a very profound way. They do not yet have the cognitive sophistication to reason analytically and ②<u>reject</u> false information. If a preschool boy consistently hears from his mother that he is smart and a good helper, he is likely to incorporate that information into his self-image. ③<u>Think</u> of himself as a boy who is smart and knows how to do things is likely to make him endure longer in problem-solving efforts and increase his confidence in trying new and difficult tasks. ④<u>Similarly</u>, thinking of himself as the kind of boy who is a good helper will make him more likely to volunteer to help with tasks at home and at preschool.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: Think → Thinking: 동명사 주어 자리에 동사 원형이 올 수 없음
det.analysis:
① available: 형용사 후치수식, tools available for — 정상
② reject: 동사원형, to reason and reject 병렬 — 정상
③ Think → Thinking: 문장 주어 자리에 동명사 필요 ←정답
④ Similarly: 문장 부사, 앞 내용과 유사성 연결 — 정상
det.tip: 동명사 주어: Thinking of himself ... is likely to ...

questions.passage: Although praise is one of the most powerful tools available for improving young children's behavior, it is equally powerful for improving your child's self-esteem. Preschoolers believe what their parents tell them in a very ①<u>profound</u> way. They do not yet have the cognitive sophistication to reason analytically and reject false information. If a preschool boy consistently hears from his mother that he is smart and a good helper, he is likely to incorporate that information into his self-image. Thinking of himself as a boy who is smart and ②<u>knowing</u> how to do things is likely to make him ③<u>endure</u> longer in problem-solving efforts and increase his confidence in trying new and difficult tasks. Similarly, thinking of himself as the kind of boy who is a good helper will make him more likely to ④<u>volunteer</u> to help with tasks at home and at preschool.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: knowing → knows: 관계절 내 동사. who is smart and knows에서 병렬 동사
det.analysis:
① profound: 형용사, a very profound way — 정상
② knowing → knows: 관계절 who절에서 is와 병렬 3인칭 단수 현재 동사 필요 ←정답
③ endure: 동사원형, make him endure 사역동사 구문 — 정상
④ volunteer: 동사원형, more likely to volunteer — 정상
det.tip: a boy who is smart and knows: 관계절 내 동사 병렬

questions.passage: Although praise is one of the most powerful tools available for ①<u>improving</u> young children's behavior, it is equally powerful for improving your child's self-esteem. Preschoolers believe ②<u>what</u> their parents tell them in a very profound way. They do not yet have the cognitive sophistication to reason analytically and reject false information. If a preschool boy consistently hears from his mother that he is smart and a good helper, he is likely to ③<u>incorporate</u> that information into his self-image. Thinking of himself as a boy who is smart and knows how to do things is likely to make him endure longer in problem-solving efforts and increase his confidence in trying new and difficult tasks. Similarly, thinking of himself as the kind of boy who is a good helper will make him ④<u>most</u> likely to volunteer to help with tasks at home and at preschool.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: most → more: 비교급 more likely가 맞는 맥락. 최상급 most는 비교 집단 없이 부적절
det.analysis:
① improving: 전치사 for 뒤 동명사 목적어 — 정상
② what: 선행사 포함 관계대명사, tell의 직접목적어 역할 — 정상
③ incorporate: be likely to + 동사원형 — 정상
④ most → more: will make him more likely에서 비교급 필요. most는 비교 대상 없이 부적절 ←정답
det.tip: more likely(비교급) vs most likely(최상급). 칭찬 전후 비교 맥락

questions.passage: Although praise is one of the most powerful tools available for improving young children's behavior, it is equally powerful for improving your child's self-esteem. Preschoolers believe what their parents tell them in a very ①<u>profound</u> way. They do not yet have the cognitive sophistication to reason analytically and ②<u>reject</u> false information. If a preschool boy consistently hears from his mother that he is ③<u>smart</u> and a good helper, he is likely to incorporate that information into his self-image. Thinking of himself as a boy who is smart and knows how to do things is likely to make him endure longer in problem-solving efforts and ④<u>undermine</u> his confidence in trying new and difficult tasks. Similarly, thinking of himself as the kind of boy who is a good helper will make him more likely to volunteer to help with tasks at home and at preschool.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: undermine(약화시키다) → increase(증가시키다): 자신감을 '증가'시키는 맥락에서 반대 방향
det.analysis:
① profound(심오한) — 부모의 말을 깊이 받아들인다는 맥락에 적절
② reject(거부하다) — 거짓 정보를 거부한다는 맥락에 적절
③ smart(똑똑한) — 어머니의 긍정적 칭찬 내용으로 적절
④ undermine → increase: 자신감 '증가'가 맞는 긍정적 맥락 ←정답
det.tip: increase(증가시키다) vs undermine(약화시키다)

questions.passage: Although praise is one of the most powerful tools available for improving young children's behavior, it is ①<u>equally</u> powerful for improving your child's self-esteem. Preschoolers believe what their parents tell them in a very profound way. They do not yet have the cognitive sophistication to reason analytically and reject false information. If a preschool boy ②<u>sporadically</u> hears from his mother that he is smart and a good helper, he is likely to ③<u>incorporate</u> that information into his self-image. Thinking of himself as a boy who is smart and knows how to do things is likely to make him endure longer in problem-solving efforts and increase his confidence in trying new and difficult tasks. Similarly, thinking of himself as the kind of boy who is a good helper will make him more likely to ④<u>volunteer</u> to help with tasks at home and at preschool.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: sporadically(산발적으로) → consistently(지속적으로): '지속적으로' 칭찬해야 자아상에 통합된다는 맥락
det.analysis:
① equally(동등하게) — 행동과 자존감 향상에 동등하게 강력하다는 맥락에 적절
② sporadically → consistently: '지속적으로' 듣는 것이 자아상 통합의 조건 ←정답
③ incorporate(통합하다) — 정보를 자아상에 통합한다는 맥락에 적절
④ volunteer(자원하다) — 자발적으로 돕게 된다는 맥락에 적절
det.tip: consistently(지속적으로) vs sporadically(산발적으로)

questions.passage: Although praise is one of the most powerful tools available for improving young children's behavior, it is equally powerful for improving your child's self-esteem. Preschoolers believe what their parents tell them in a very profound way. They do not yet have the cognitive sophistication to __________ and reject false information. If a preschool boy consistently hears from his mother that he is smart and a good helper, he is likely to incorporate that information into his self-image. Thinking of himself as a boy who is smart and knows how to do things is likely to make him endure longer in problem-solving efforts and increase his confidence in trying new and difficult tasks. Similarly, thinking of himself as the kind of boy who is a good helper will make him more likely to volunteer to help with tasks at home and at preschool.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: reason analytically(분석적으로 추론하다) — 미취학 아동이 갖추지 못한 인지 능력
det.analysis:
① think independently(독립적으로 사고하다) — 본문에 없는 표현
② communicate effectively(효과적으로 소통하다) — 인지 추론이 아닌 의사소통
③ reason analytically(분석적으로 추론하다) — and reject false information과 병렬 ←정답
④ behave appropriately(적절하게 행동하다) — 행동이 아닌 인지 능력 맥락
det.tip: the cognitive sophistication to _____ and reject: 병렬 구조

questions.passage: Although praise is one of the most powerful tools available for improving young children's behavior, it is equally powerful for improving your child's self-esteem. Preschoolers believe what their parents tell them __________. They do not yet have the cognitive sophistication to reason analytically and reject false information. If a preschool boy consistently hears from his mother that he is smart and a good helper, he is likely to incorporate that information into his self-image. Thinking of himself as a boy who is smart and knows how to do things is likely to make him endure longer in problem-solving efforts and increase his confidence in trying new and difficult tasks. Similarly, thinking of himself as the kind of boy who is a good helper will make him more likely to volunteer to help with tasks at home and at preschool.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: in a very profound way(매우 심오한 방식으로) — 부모의 말을 깊이 있게 받아들이는 방식
det.analysis:
① in a relatively critical way(비판적) — 비판 능력 없다고 함. 반대
② in a very profound way(심오한) — 깊이 믿음 + 인지 미성숙 근거 ←정답
③ in a somewhat skeptical way(회의적) — 회의적이면 거짓 정보 거부 가능. 반대
④ in a highly selective way(선택적) — 선택적 = 거짓 정보 거부 가능. 반대
det.tip: profound → 다음 문장: 인지적 정교함 부족으로 거짓 정보 거부 불가

questions.passage: Although praise is one of the most powerful tools available for improving young children's behavior, it is equally powerful for improving your child's self-esteem. Preschoolers believe what their parents tell them in a very profound way. They do not yet have the cognitive sophistication to reason analytically and reject false information. If a preschool boy consistently hears from his mother that he is smart and a good helper, he is likely to incorporate that information into his self-image. Thinking of himself as a boy who is smart and knows how to do things is likely to make him endure longer in problem-solving efforts and increase his confidence in trying new and difficult tasks. Similarly, thinking of himself as the kind of boy who is a good helper will make him more likely to volunteer to help with tasks at home and at preschool.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: 칭찬 → 자아상 → 행동 변화라는 본문 전체 흐름과 일치
det.analysis:
① 행동 개선에만 효과 — equally powerful for self-esteem. 오답
② 거짓 정보를 걸러냄 — do not yet have ... to reject. 오답
③ 쉬운 과제만 선호 — trying new and difficult tasks. 오답
④ 자아상이 행동에 영향 — incorporate → endure + volunteer ←정답
det.tip: 칭찬 → 자아상 형성 → 행동 변화

ch: 칭찬은 아이의 행동 개선에만 효과가 있다.
미취학 아동은 거짓 정보를 스스로 걸러낸다.
자신이 똑똑하다고 생각하는 아이는 쉬운 과제만 선호한다.
칭찬을 통해 형성된 자아상은 아이의 행동에 영향을 미친다.

questions.passage: Although praise is one of the most powerful tools available for improving young children's behavior, it is equally powerful for improving your child's self-esteem. Preschoolers believe what their parents tell them in a very profound way. They do not yet have the cognitive sophistication to reason analytically and reject false information. If a preschool boy consistently hears from his mother that he is smart and a good helper, he is likely to incorporate that information into his self-image. Thinking of himself as a boy who is smart and knows how to do things is likely to make him endure longer in problem-solving efforts and increase his confidence in trying new and difficult tasks. Similarly, thinking of himself as the kind of boy who is a good helper will make him more likely to volunteer to help with tasks at home and at preschool.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: '가끔' → 본문은 'consistently(지속적으로)'. 빈도 왜곡
det.analysis:
① 가끔 칭찬 → consistently(지속적으로). 빈도 왜곡 ←정답
② 자존감에도 강력한 효과 → equally powerful. 일치
③ 깊이 있게 받아들임 → in a very profound way. 일치
④ 자발적으로 돕기 → volunteer to help. 일치
det.tip: consistently(지속적으로) ≠ 가끔

ch: 소년이 어머니에게 가끔 칭찬을 들으면 그 정보를 자아상에 통합한다.
칭찬은 어린 아이의 자존감 향상에도 강력한 효과가 있다.
미취학 아동은 부모의 말을 깊이 있게 받아들인다.
착한 도우미라는 자아상을 가진 아이는 집과 유치원에서 자발적으로 돕는다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: 자신이 똑똑하다는 자아상이 문제 해결 과정에서 더 오래 견디게 만든다
det.analysis:
① 분석적 사고 발달 — do not yet have. 반대. 오답
② 자아상에 영향 없음 — incorporate into self-image. 반대. 오답
③ 더 오래 견딤 — make him endure longer. 일치 ←정답
④ 도움 거부 — more likely to volunteer. 반대. 오답
det.tip: endure longer in problem-solving efforts

ch: 미취학 아동은 분석적 사고 능력이 충분히 발달해 있다.
어머니의 칭찬은 아이의 자아상 형성에 별다른 영향을 주지 않는다.
자신이 똑똑하다는 자아상은 문제 해결에서 더 오래 견디게 한다.
착한 도우미로 생각하는 아이는 도움 요청을 거부할 가능성이 높다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 부모의 칭찬이 미취학 아동의 자아상과 행동에 미치는 긍정적 영향
det.analysis:
① 인지 능력 발달 — 배경 설명일 뿐, 주제 아님
② 칭찬이 자아상과 행동에 미치는 영향 — 본문 전체 흐름 ←정답
③ 문제 해결 교육 — 칭찬의 결과 중 하나일 뿐
④ 사회성 전략 — 또래 관계 언급 없음
det.tip: praise → self-image → behavior 흐름

ch: 미취학 아동의 인지 능력 발달과 한계
부모의 칭찬이 아이의 자아상과 행동에 미치는 영향
어린이의 문제 해결 능력을 키우는 교육 방법

questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 긍정적 언어 강화 = praise, 자기인식 = self-image, 행동 = endure/volunteer
det.analysis:
① 인지적 미성숙의 부정적 효과 — 배경 설명, 부정적 효과 서술 아님
② 의사소통 방식 — '칭찬'이라는 구체적 도구에 초점
③ 자존감과 또래 관계 — 또래 관계 언급 없음
④ 긍정적 언어 강화 → 자기인식 + 행동 형성 — 추상적 패러프레이즈 ←정답
det.tip: praise→긍정적 언어 강화, self-image→자기인식

ch: 아이의 인지적 미성숙이 학습에 미치는 부정적 효과
부모와 자녀 간 의사소통 방식의 중요성
미취학 아동의 자존감과 또래 관계의 상관성
긍정적 언어 강화가 미취학 아동의 자기인식과 행동을 형성하는 과정

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 incorporate that information into his self-image가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 부모의 긍정적 평가를 자기 정체성의 일부로 내면화하다
det.analysis:
① 일시적 기억 — incorporate는 '통합/내면화'이지 '일시적 저장' 아님

③ 긍정적 평가를 정체성 일부로 받아들이다 — incorporate + self-image 정확한 함축 ←정답

자신의 행동을 다른 아이들과 비교하여 평가하다
